sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Evolutionary Hierarchy**: The office evolved from **Governor of Bengal** (1773) to **Governor-General of Bengal** (1773), **Governor-General of India** (1833), and **Viceroy** (1858).
• **Dual Role Post-1858**: The Viceroy acted as the **Representative of the Crown** (Viceroy) and the **Head of the Executive Council** (Governor-General).
• **Legislative Supremacy**: The **Indian Councils Act 1861** introduced the **Portfolio System** by Lord Canning, formalizing departmental administration.
• **Key Metric**: The shift from 'Commercial' (EIC) to 'Imperial' (Crown) governance changed the focus from profit-maximization to administrative consolidation and control.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Warren Hastings to Bentinck; focused on EIC consolidation.
Bentinck to Canning; centralized legislative power.
Canning to Mountbatten; direct Crown rule.
Mains: Impact of policies on Indian Nationalism.

items.definition: Introduced by Lord Canning (1861); allowed members of the Executive Council to be in charge of specific departments (Home, Revenue, Military, etc.).
Policy by Lord Dalhousie; annexed states where the ruler died without a natural heir, directly contributing to the 1857 Revolt.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Administrative**: Introduction of Civil Services (Cornwallis), Police reforms, and Judicial codification.
• **Socio-Religious**: Abolition of Sati (Bentinck), Widow Remarriage Act (Dalhousie/Canning).

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Balancing British imperial interests with rising Indian nationalist aspirations.
• **Solutions**: Gradual devolution of power via Morley-Minto, Mont-Ford reforms.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'W-C-W-B-D-C' (Early GGs: Warren, Cornwallis, Wellesley, Bentinck, Dalhousie, Canning).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Warren (Hastings), Cornwallis (Permanent Settlement), Wellesley (Subsidiary Alliance), Bentinck (Social Reforms), Dalhousie (Lapse), Canning (1857 Revolt).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: Confusing the 'Governor-General of Bengal' (1773) with 'Governor-General of India' (1833). Warren Hastings was the first GG of Bengal; William Bentinck was the first GG of India.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Administrative Centralization' for the period 1833-1861 and 'Decentralization' for the period post-1861.

keyTakeaways: 1773 Act created the office of Governor-General of Bengal.
1833 Act created the office of Governor-General of India.
1858 Act created the office of Viceroy of India.
